sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Nottingham Forest host Aston Villa at the City Ground. Forest are 16th (32 points), Villa are 4th (54 points). The Sofascore model rates outcomes as: home win 22%, draw 29%, away win 49%, with 39% for both teams to score.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Forest are unbeaten in 4 (W2 D2) and won 3-0 at Tottenham, though they were out-created in the 1-1 draw at Porto (expected goals 0.45 vs 2.16). Villa have 3 wins in their last 5, including 2-0 vs West Ham and 2-0 vs Lille, plus a 3-1 away win at Bologna.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Villa won the last 2 meetings at Villa Park (3-1, 2-1), with John McGinn influential. Recent meetings have produced goals, but the model’s 39% for both teams to score points to a lower likelihood this time.

sections.subtitle: Season stats
sections.text: Forest’s attack ranks 19th for goals (31) and 18th for big chances created (50), but their defence is mid-table for goals conceded (43). They average 82% passing accuracy and 5.35 corners per game.

sections.subtitle: Tactical notes and key players
sections.text: Forest rely on Morgan Gibbs-White (9 goals) and service from wide areas via Neco Williams. Villa’s threat is led by Ollie Watkins (4 goals in last 5), with Morgan Rogers and John McGinn adding creativity and runs from midfield.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Michael Salisbury averages 3.3 yellow cards and 0.20 reds per game. Both sides trend to fewer than 4.5 cards, and head-to-head corners have stayed under 10.5 in recent meetings; Forest average 5.35 corners.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Villa are more likely to take points, with the model favouring an away win. Forest’s recent resilience narrows the gap, but Villa’s form and first-goal trend support the visitors. Lower probability for both teams to score aligns with the model.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Half-time at the City Ground and it is 1-1. Aston Villa led through a Murillo own goal (23'), before Neco Williams equalised for Nottingham Forest (38'). The numbers point to a balanced game with contrasting strengths: Aston Villa have edged possession (53-47) and aerial duels (63%), while Nottingham Forest have carried the greater direct threat in the box (shots on target 4-0, penalty area entries 18-12). Corners favour Nottingham Forest (4-1). Expected goals are low on both sides (Nottingham Forest 0.35, Aston Villa 0.20), but Aston Villa did hit the woodwork once.

halftimeSections.subtitle: First-half summary
halftimeSections.text: Nottingham Forest were more efficient at turning build-up into box actions, helped by regains high up the pitch (possessions won in the final third 7-2). Williams was the key outlet, producing 3 shots on target and the equaliser, with Callum Hudson-Odoi supplying the assist and 3 key passes. Aston Villa controlled territory (final third entries 28-21) and duels (55% won), but they lacked shots on target despite one effort against the frame and decent crossing positions.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Nottingham Forest started with brief pressure, but Aston Villa grew into the game and put together their strongest spell around the mid-20s. After a further away surge just before the equaliser, the momentum flipped decisively towards Nottingham Forest from the goal through to half-time, with sustained pressure up to the whistle.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical notes and adjustments
halftimeSections.text:
Nottingham Forest should keep targeting quick transitions and the right channel where Williams found space. Their counter-press has been effective; maintaining pressure on Aston Villa’s first pass after turnovers can sustain territory and create second-phase shots. Set plays have yielded territory, but with Aston Villa stronger in the air, Nottingham Forest may profit more from second balls rather than direct aerial wins.
Aston Villa need to convert territorial control into clearer chances by accelerating switches to wide areas and delivering earlier crosses to exploit their aerial edge. They must also protect rest defence against counters, as Nottingham Forest’s 7 high regains indicate vulnerability when Aston Villa lose the ball in midfield.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key player performances
halftimeSections.text:
Nottingham Forest: Neco Williams (goal, 3 shots on target, strong forward runs), Callum Hudson-Odoi (1 assist, 3 key passes), Murillo (own goal but active defensively with clearances). Morgan Gibbs-White registered 1 shot on target and remains a threat between the lines.
Aston Villa: Youri Tielemans and John McGinn have been tidy in progression and chance creation (each with a key pass contribution), Lucas Digne provides width and set-piece delivery, while Amadou Onana has competed well in duels. Ollie Watkins has been quiet and needs better service into the area.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: Bookings are level (Nottingham Forest 1, Aston Villa 1), suggesting a competitive but controlled game. Corners currently favour Nottingham Forest (4-1). Expect the card count to remain moderate unless the game state becomes more volatile. If the pattern holds, Nottingham Forest are slightly more likely to finish ahead on corners, though Aston Villa’s aerial strength could earn them more set plays if they increase sustained pressure.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: The game is finely poised. Nottingham Forest’s transitions and right-side combinations look the clearest route to chances, while Aston Villa’s path lies in quicker ball circulation and exploiting wide-to-box deliveries. Given the low expected goals and Aston Villa’s lack of shots on target so far, the second half may be tight, with phases of control for both sides. Small margins at set plays and the first big chance after the restart could decide it.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: A balanced, low-margin second half. Nottingham Forest’s transitions have been the sharper weapon, but Aston Villa’s territorial control and aerial advantage keep them in it. Prediction: it remains level at 1-1.
